title: Dad Don’t Read This by Eliya Smith at St Luke’s Theatre #amaliayoo #d...
transcript: Fresh off of John Proctor Is The Villain, Amalia Yoo stars in a new play by Eliya Smith that I'd consider part of the same extended family. Another ensemble piece that deals with teenage angst, Dad Don't Read This is a quirky and funny portrait of four friends navigating what it feels like to not really know anything. A central element is the video game The Sims, a stand-in for the agency they crave but can't find in their real lives. They also find comfort in a simulated world where stakes are low and empathy is irrelevant since consequences are nonexistent. Much like The Sims, this play is neatly contained. Though the characters are grappling with big and complicated feelings, oscillating between crippling insecurity and ruthless arrogance as so many teenagers do, they're all remarkably specific. The strong performances from the entire ensemble prevent the script from having to do any heavy lifting in terms of exposition. It also leaves room for ambiguity that's interesting rather than frustrating. For example, Mal has been missing at lunchtime for weeks and her parents are always fighting. Something's going on, but we don't really know what her deal is. It's a depiction of teenage resistance to being seen, through naturally captivating scene work that also shows how quickly teenagers turn from friendly to vicious. Overall, I found it a perfectly succinct 90 minutes, an easy watch that still left me with plenty to chew on. Dad Don’t Read This is running now at St Luke's Theatre. With that, another program for my collection.
